drill_name: Grip Check — Find It Without Looking
teaching_job: Finding and checking the grip as its own repeatable rep, rather than as one clause inside a stance drill.
why_not_a_duplicate: Searched all 47 Hitting, 3 Soft Toss and 3 Bunting rows. Exactly one carries "grip" in mechanic_focus — the stance drill, where grip is one of five things it trains and gets one clause of set-up and one mastery signal.

drill_name: Pick Your Hop — Read It and Move to It
teaching_job: Choosing the hop: reading the ball early, counting hops, and moving the feet to create a long hop or a short one rather than fielding whatever arrives.
why_not_a_duplicate: All 20 Fielding (Infield) rows checked. Recovery Drill trains recovery after a misplay; Advanced First Base trains short-hop picks at the bag; Wall Ball gives solo short hops. None trains hop selection — the charge-or-drop-back decision — and no mechanic_focus in the category mentions reading or counting hops.

drill_name: Ready and Go — Outfield First Step
teaching_job: Pre-pitch ready position and a first movement in any direction from a standing start.
why_not_a_duplicate: The drop-step drill trains the first step for balls hit overhead only. On the Run starts the fielder already moving, which is why it cannot teach the start. The priority drill lists ready position in mechanic_focus but its teaching job is who calls the ball.

drill_name: Routine Outfield Ground Ball — Field It and Come Up Throwing
teaching_job: The routine outfield ground ball — get around it, field it in the middle of the body, come up into the throw — and the knee-down block when nobody is advancing.
why_not_a_duplicate: Do-or-Die is the only outfield ground-ball drill and it is explicitly the highest-urgency version — attack angle, glove-side pickup, momentum through the throw. Four Cones is infield-framed and attached here as a regression for the approach alone.

drill_name: Changeup Off the Mound — Same Arm Speed, Real Sequence
teaching_job: Throwing the second pitch from the mound, in sequence with the fastball, to a hitter.
why_not_a_duplicate: One changeup drill exists and it is catch play — grip and arm speed on flat ground. Nothing takes the pitch onto a mound or puts it in a sequence, and the stage is served by a single row.

drill_name: Catcher's Stance — Set Up to Receive
teaching_job: The stance itself — how a catcher sets up before any pitch is received.
why_not_a_duplicate: The brief floats Quiet Hands Receiving; the library already has it, named Quiet Glove & Soft Hands, and it is this stage's primary. What is absent is the stance: all six Catching rows assume a catcher already crouched. The stage's second drill is Two Hand Catch, borrowed from Throwing.
